title: Kiosk client registration and tokens (OAuth)
description: The wire objects of Section 5: RFC 7591 open client registration of the AI assistant's public key, RFC 7523 client assertions signed with that key (the private_key_jwt method), and DPoP-bound access tokens from the client_credentials grant (RFC 9449). The roots are open: they state what MUST be present and the shape of each member.

publicJwk.description: Section 5.1 -- the AI assistant's public key as an RFC 7517 JWK: an Ed25519 key (RFC 8037), or a P-256 key where the operator accepts ES256. A member that only a private key has is refused. Other members (kid, use, alg) are allowed and ignored.

kty.description: The key type: OKP for an Ed25519 key, which signs EdDSA; EC for a P-256 key, which signs ES256.

crv.description: The curve: Ed25519 for OKP, P-256 for EC.

x.description: The base64url public key of an OKP key, or the base64url x coordinate of an EC key.

y.description: The base64url y coordinate of an EC key.

jwks.description: Section 5.1 -- an RFC 7517 JWK Set that holds exactly one key, the AI assistant's public key.

registrationRequest.description: Section 5.1 -- the body of POST <endpoint>/oauth/register, an RFC 7591 open registration: no initial access token and no human. The operator ignores every member it does not know (RFC 7591 Section 2). An optional proof-of-work proof rides in the `Kiosk-PoW` request header, never in this body.

token_endpoint_auth_method.description: The one client authentication method: a client assertion signed with the registered key (RFC 7523).

grant_types.description: A subset of the grant types this origin serves. The operator registers the client for every grant type it serves and answers that list.

clientInformation.description: Section 5.1 -- the 201 answer to POST <endpoint>/oauth/register (RFC 7591 Section 3.2.1), and the 200 answer to POST <endpoint>/auth/rotate (Section 5.7). Registering a key that is registered already answers the same client again.

client_id.description: The client identifier. It is also the `agent_id` of the assistant account, stable across a rotation and a rebind.

client_id_issued_at.description: When the client was registered, in Unix seconds.

grant_types.description: `client_credentials`, and the device-code grant where the origin serves account binding.

dpop_bound_access_tokens.description: RFC 9449 Section 5.2: every token request carries a DPoP proof.

registrationError.description: Section 5.1 -- the 400 answer of POST <endpoint>/oauth/register (RFC 7591 Section 3.2.2). The toll on registration answers with problem documents instead (Section 10).

error.description: The one registration error code: a member of the request is missing or not valid.

error_description.description: Human-readable detail. An AI assistant branches on `error` and never on this string.

clientAssertion.description: Section 5.2 -- the decoded payload of a client assertion (RFC 7523 Section 3), a compact JWS that the registered key signs. It is sent as `client_assertion`, with `client_assertion_type` = `urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer`. It is a PAYLOAD, not a request body.

sub.description: The client_id, the same value as `iss`.

aud.description: ORIGIN-BINDING. The issuer of the origin the AI assistant dialed, as its only value (Section 15.1). A string, or an array with that one string.

exp.description: Expiry. The operator refuses an assertion that has expired or that expires more than 300 seconds after its clock.

jti.description: A unique id. The operator accepts each id of a client one time.

tokenResponse.description: Section 5.3 -- the 200 answer of POST <endpoint>/oauth/token (RFC 6749 Section 5.1), for the client_credentials grant and for the device-code grant (Section 6.1). The principal (`user_id`, `agent_id`) is in the access token's claims.

access_token.description: The access token, a compact EdDSA JWT. Its claims are `#/$defs/accessTokenClaims`.

token_type.description: Always "DPoP": the token is bound to the registered key (Section 5.6).

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token expires.

scope.description: The role of the assistant account, as the scope that RFC 6749 Section 5.1 grants. It is present only when the account has a role, and never null. An AI assistant MUST NOT treat its absence as an error.

oauthError.description: Sections 5.3 and 6.1 -- the error answer of POST <endpoint>/oauth/token and POST <endpoint>/oauth/device_authorization (RFC 6749 Section 5.2). The status is 400 for every code except `invalid_client`, which is 401. The toll answers with problem documents instead (Section 6.4).

error.description: The OAuth error code: four of RFC 6749 Section 5.2, `invalid_dpop_proof` of RFC 9449, and the four device-grant codes of RFC 8628 Section 3.5. A closed vocabulary: an operator MUST NOT emit a code outside it.

error_description.description: Human-readable detail. An AI assistant branches on `error` and never on this string.

accessTokenClaims.description: Section 5.4 -- the decoded claim set of `access_token`. A 3-part EdDSA JWT signed by the operator and verifiable statelessly against the JWKS of Section 4.4, bound to the identity's key and presented as `Authorization: DPoP` with a DPoP proof (Section 5.6).

actor.description: Always the string "agent". A token minted for anything else is not a Kiosk access token.

role.description: The role the operator assigns (Section 5.4). It is omitted when absent, never null. No endpoint accepts a role that the client requests.

aud.description: The operator issuer. A string, or the array spelling RFC 7519 permits.

iat.description: Issued-at. Also what the revoked-before watermark of Section 15.4 is compared against.

exp.description: Expiry. Default lifetime is 1 hour; the durable credential is the private key, not the token.

cnf.description: RFC 9449 Section 6.1 -- the key the token is bound to. Only a DPoP proof that this key signs makes the token usable.

jkt.description: The RFC 7638 thumbprint of the registered key.

dpopProof.description: Section 5.6 -- the decoded payload of the `DPoP` request header, a compact JWS whose header carries `typ: "dpop+jwt"`, the `alg` of the registered key (EdDSA, or ES256) and its public `jwk`. The AI assistant signs a new one for each token request and for each request that carries an access token.

jti.description: A unique id for this proof.

htm.description: The HTTP method of the request.

htu.description: The URL of the request, with no query and no fragment. On the event stream it is `events_url` with `wss` written as `https`.

iat.description: The time of signing. The operator refuses a proof more than 60 seconds from its clock.

ath.description: The base64url SHA-256 of the ASCII access token, with no padding. REQUIRED on a request that carries an access token; absent on a token request.

rotationAssertion.description: Section 5.7 -- the decoded payload of `client_assertion` in a rotation: a client assertion by the registered key that also names the new key.

new_key.description: The RFC 7638 thumbprint of the new key in `jwks`.

rotationRequest.description: Section 5.7 -- the body of POST <endpoint>/auth/rotate, a Kiosk extension. The answer is `#/$defs/clientInformation` with the new key; the AI assistant then asks the token endpoint for a token with the new key.

client_assertion.description: A client assertion by the registered key. Its decoded payload is `#/$defs/rotationAssertion`.

new_client_assertion.description: A client assertion by the new key, for the same client_id. Its decoded payload is `#/$defs/clientAssertion`.
